s5-2.title: History: The Babylonian Co-Regency Hierarchy (Adult Sabbath School Bible Study Guide, 2020 Q1, Lesson 6)

steps.title: Nabonidus
steps.text: History: King of Babylon, residing in Tema, Arabia (Bible Commentary, vol. 4, on Daniel 5:1). ABC 7: The king (was) in Tayma.
steps.detail: The Nabonidus Chronicle places the king in Tayma while the city is governed in his name, and the Verse Account agrees. That absence is the reason a second man can hold the throne room on the night the writing appears.

steps.title: Belshazzar
steps.text: History: Eldest son, Co-regent ruling inside Babylon (Bible Commentary, vol. 4, on Daniel 5).
steps.detail: He offers the third place in the kingdom, not the second, and that is the detail the co-regency explains. In Daniel 5:7 the reward is to be the third ruler, which is what a son ruling under an absent father could actually grant.

steps.title: Daniel
steps.detail: The reward is proclaimed and Daniel is clothed in scarlet the same night the city falls, and he takes it without asking for it. By morning the empire that offered it has changed hands.

cells: NUMBERED: God has numbered your kingdom and finished it.
WEIGHED: You are weighed on the scales and found wanting.
DIVIDED: Your kingdom is divided and given to the Medo-Persians.
